Article Title: Gujarat UCC Bill gets President Murmu’s nod paving way for implementation
Article Text:
President Murmu gives assent to Gujarat UCC Bill, state becomes second after Uttarakhand

NEW DELHI: President Droupadi Murmu has given her assent to the Gujarat Uniform Civil Code Bill, 2026, completing the key legal process required for the state to enact the law.The Gujarat assembly had earlier passed the Gujarat Uniform Civil Code Bill, 2026, making the state the second in India after Uttarakhand to pass legislation seeking to implement a Uniform Civil Code. However, the provisions of the bill will not apply to members of Scheduled Tribes (STs).While tabling the bill in the Assembly, chief minister Bhupendra Patel had said that the UCC was among the key reforms that Prime Minister Narendra Modi was determined to implement. "The key aim of introducing the bill is to ensure social harmony and national unity. The Supreme Court has also suggested that UCC will ensure women's rights are secured," the CM said.The bill proposes mandatory registration of marriages and divorces, with a fine of up to Rs 10,000 for non-compliance.It also makes registration of all live-in relationships compulsory, while requiring couples to notify authorities when such relationships end. Children born from live-in relationships will be considered legitimate children of the couple, while women deserted by their live-in partners will be entitled to seek maintenance, according to the bill.The legislation bans polygamy and provides for up to seven years' imprisonment for marriages conducted through coercion or force. Divorce through any means other than a court decree will be punishable with up to three years in prison.The bill also allows divorced couples to remarry without conditions and prohibits the practice of `halala' in certain communities.
Article Summary: President Droupadi Murmu has given her assent to the Gujarat Uniform Civil Code Bill, 2026. Bill proposes mandatory registration of marriages and divorces, with a fine of up to Rs 10,000 for non-compliance. Bill also allows divorced couples to remarry without conditions and prohibits the practice of `halala'

Article Title: Centre identifies 28 spots in Ladakh for inclusion on official Survey of India map
Article Text:
28 spots identified in Ladakh for inclusion on official Survey of India map

Standard names for Ladakh’s geographical features

Gogra, Hot Spring among identified features

NEW DELHI: The Centre has identified and standardised 28 places and geographical features in Ladakh by their official place and feature names for inclusion on the Survey of India (SoI) map, the Ministry of Home Affairs said on Thursday.The exercise was carried out in consultation with the Union Territory administration of Ladakh and is aimed at ensuring accurate recognition of the locations and creating greater awareness about them, the ministry said, news agency ANI reported.The 28 identified locations include peaks, mountains, passes, glaciers, valleys, rivers, lakes, water bodies and land areas.The list includes Atisha Giri, Kanishka Peak, Martand Giri, Zorawar Peak, Rinchen Zangpo, Sakyasri Giri, Marpa Lotsava Ri, Milarepa Kangri, Shiva Ri and Maheshvara Ri among the peaks.Karun Pir, Drak Karpo and Jolmori have been identified as mountains, while Chapchingal Pass and Shachmirk Pass have been designated as passes. Parpik and Skamri have been identified as glaciers, while Shkorga Valley and Yangpa River are also among the features formally recorded.The list also includes Gogra, Dehra Compass, Brangsa, Kuksel, Kumarayana Point, Panglung and Shamal Lungpa as land areas. Guru Rinpoche has been identified as a lake, while Hot Spring has been listed as a water body.The standardisation of geographical names is part of maintaining official cartographic records and ensuring consistency in the names used for geographical features across government maps and records.The exercise also covers strategically significant locations in Ladakh, including Gogra and Hot Spring, which were among the friction points during the India-China border standoff in eastern Ladakh.The Survey of India, the country's national mapping agency, is responsible for surveying, mapping and preparing official maps of India. The formal inclusion of the 28 locations is expected to provide standard references for the features and improve public awareness of their names and locations.
Article Summary: The Centre has identified and standardised 28 places and geographical features in Ladakh by their official place and feature names. The exercise was carried out in consultation with the Union Territory administration of Ladakh. The 28 identified locations include peaks, mountains, passes, glaciers, valleys, rivers, lakes and land areas.

NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Friday launched the expanded 'Vettri Payanam Thittam', extending free bus travel to more categories of services for women and transgender people across the state.Marking the launch on Gandhi Jayanti, Vijay travelled by bus in Chennai, interacted with passengers and personally handed out free tickets to women.In a light-hearted moment, college students travelling on the bus were also seen sharing Dairy Milk chocolates with the chief minister.The expanded scheme is expected to benefit around 84.32 lakh women every day. Beneficiaries can travel free of cost on 12,695 buses operated by seven state transport corporations, including services in the express and deluxe categories.There is no income ceiling to avail the scheme and no limit on the number of trips a beneficiary can make in a day, the state government said.The scheme, whose name is derived from the ruling Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK), meaning “victorious journey”, was earlier limited to certain categories of buses. The expanded facility now covers express, deluxe, mofussil ordinary and certain Ghat-area services.Earlier, transport minister A Vijay Tamilan Parthiban said the scheme aims to support the education, employment, livelihoods and economic empowerment of women and transgender people by ensuring that transportation costs do not become a barrier to their progress.He said the initiative was also aimed at promoting equality, adding that there should be no distinction in travel rights.Parthiban described the scheme as a “social revolution” that would help women become more independent, step out of their homes and contribute to the state’s growth."The launch is also meant to honour the principles of social justice and women's empowerment, to facilitate their participation in the economy and society, ensuring that transportation costs do not hinder their access to education, employment, or healthcare," the minister added.
Article Summary: The expanded scheme is expected to benefit around 84.32 lakh women every day. Beneficiaries can travel free of cost on 12,695 buses operated by seven state transport corporations. NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Wednesday said that he had a "productive conversation" with US President Donald Trump and reviewed bilateral cooperation between New Delhi and Washington in various sectors.In a social media post on X, PM Modi said the leaders agreed to maintain close engagement to take their Comprehensive Global Strategic Partnership forward."Had a productive conversation with President Trump. We reviewed our bilateral cooperation in trade, defence, energy, critical technologies and other areas. We agreed to maintain close engagement to take our Comprehensive Global Strategic Partnership forward," PM Modi said."We also exchanged views on regional and international issues, including ongoing efforts to advance global peace and security," he added.The two leaders agreed to remain in touch as both sides continue to deepen the strategic partnership.This comes days after Trump signed into law a sweeping sanctions package targeting Russia and Iran and giving his administration expanded powers to penalise countries that continue buying Russian oil and gas, including India.The legislation is particularly significant for India because it gives Trump the authority to impose tariffs of up to 100 per cent on imports from the five largest buyers of Russian oil or natural gas.India and China are among the major purchasers of Russian crude.Earlier in September, the ministry of external affairs warned the US of the legislation's potential impact on the US-India relationship."This issue has been discussed at high levels in recent months with various US interlocutors. Its potential implications for not just the bilateral relationship but also the international energy market have been very clearly articulated by the Indian side," the ministry had said.
Article Summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi says he had a "productive conversation" with US President Donald Trump. Article Title: Delhi riots case: High court rejects bail pleas Of Umar Khalid, Sharjeel Imam
Article Text:
Umar Khalid, Sharjeel Imam denied bail by high court

NEW DELHI: The Delhi High Court has refused to grant bail to Umar Khalid and Sharjeel Imam in the UAPA case related to the 2020 Delhi riots.Senior Advocate Trideep Pais, appearing for Umar Khalid, submitted that there had been three “small changes in circumstances” since the earlier proceedings. He also referred the court to a Supreme Court judgment in support of his submissions.Pais pointed out that charges have not yet been framed in the case and, consequently, prosecution witnesses are yet to be examined. The court also noted that the charges were yet to be framed.Pais further submitted that a Special Leave Petition (SLP) is pending before the Supreme Court and that the trial court has indicated it would await the Supreme Court’s order. He then continued his submissions by referring to the Supreme Court judgment.Khalid and Imam had approached the Delhi High Court earlier this year after their bail applications were dismissed by the trial court for the third time on July 4. Imam was arrested in the case on August 25, 2020, while Khalid was arrested on September 13, 2020.The Delhi Police has opposed their bail pleas in the high court, asserting that the two were “masterminds” of the riots, PTI reported.The police argued that they could not seek bail on parity with other co-accused, stating that the Supreme Court had earlier categorised them as being part of the “command authority” and held that their “risk profiles” justified “continuing detention”.The police also argued that the present bail pleas were in the teeth of the Supreme Court’s January 5 order, which directed them to seek release only after the examination of protected witnesses was completed or after one year, whichever was earlier.On July 4, the trial court rejected Khalid’s bail application, saying it had “no option but to follow” the Supreme Court’s January 5 order and could therefore neither entertain the plea nor grant him relief.On September 2, 2025, a Delhi High Court division bench denied bail to Khalid and Imam. The Supreme Court upheld the verdict on January 5 but granted relief to co-accused Gulfisha Fatima, Meeran Haider, Shifa Ur Rehman, Mohammad Saleem Khan and Shadab Ahmad.A bench of Justice Aravind Kumar and Justice NV Anjaria had observed that there was a prima facie case against Khalid and Imam under the UAPA.On May 22, the Supreme Court granted six months’ interim bail to co-accused Abdul Khalid Saifi and Tasleem Ahmad, while referring to a larger bench the issue of prolonged incarceration of undertrials under the UAPA due to the stringent conditions for granting bail.
Article Summary: Delhi High Court refuses to grant bail to Umar Khalid and Sharjeel Imam in the UAPA case related to the 2020 Delhi riots. Delhi Police has opposed their bail pleas in the high court, asserting that the two were “masterminds” of the riots.

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court has declined to meet the parliamentary committee, which is examining a Constitution amendment bill proposing simultaneous elections, saying it will not be desirable for senior judges to discuss the matter as the proposed amendment might become a subject matter of judicial review.A communication from the secretary general of the Supreme Court to the committee said the proposal for an informal discussion by the joint committee to examine Constitution (129th Amendment) Bill, 2024, and the UT Laws (Amendments Bill, 2024) on the subject of simultaneous elections with Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and other judges on Oct 6 was discussed among the senior judges.A communication from the secretary general of SC said, “They are of the opinion that as the proposed amendment might become a subject matter of judicial review before SC, it may not be expedient or desirable to discuss the issue on the administrative side. The proposed meeting is accordingly cancelled.”As SC declined, the committee, which is headed by BJP MP P P Chaudhary, wrote to its members that the scheduled meeting has been cancelled.Opposition MP Kapil Sibal had criticised the proposed meeting, suggesting that it was a violation of the doctrine of separation of powers.The bill, which proposes simultaneous Lok Sabha and assembly polls, was introduced in the Lok Sabha in Dec 2024 and was sent to the committee. Opposition parties are critical of the bill, alleging that it is unconstitutional and violates federal rights.BJP and its allies have, however, backed the idea, saying a continuous cycle of elections hampers development, and simultaneous elections will also boost economic growth.

Article Title: ‘Portal not in accordance with law’: Congress accuses Election Commission of ‘lying’ over ECINet

Congress MP Jairam Ramesh; CEC Gyanesh Kumar

NEW DELHI: The Congress on Friday accused the Election Commission (EC) of “lying” about its ECINet portal, alleging that the platform was not in accordance with the law.Congress MP Jairam Ramesh also questioned the "intentions" of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar, describing them as “not honest.”“In its damage-control but actually damage-enhancing press note on September 26, 2026, the Election Commission of India had promised a committee to certify that the legally suspect ECINet ‘complies with the provisions of the Acts and Rules’. In reality, this should never have been in doubt at all in the first place if the intentions of the CEC Gyanesh Kumar were honest—which they were not,” Ramesh wrote on X.He was referring to the poll panel’s statement last week, issued days after The Indian Express reported that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had objected on record at least 14 times over the previous 10 months to decisions and orders related to the Special Intensive Revision (SIR), which they maintained had been issued without their knowledge or recommendation.“ECINet was launched on January 22, 2026, with much fanfare to ‘enhance transparency, credibility and public trust’. The ECI press note issued that day assured the country that it ‘has been developed in strict accordance with the law’ and in full compliance with the Constitution of India, the Representation of the People Acts, 1950 and 1951, and the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960,” Ramesh wrote.“All of this was a lie,” he added.Ramesh further accused the EC of "violating" laws governing the electoral process.“By restricting Electoral Registration Officers’ (EROs) access to the ECINet voter-roll system and overruling EROs in states such as Goa and West Bengal, among others, the ECI under the CEC has violated the Representation of the People Act, 1950, and the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960. Both laws establish that EROs have statutory authority over electoral rolls,” he posted.The Congress-led opposition INDIA bloc on Wednesday announced joint “Save Democracy” marches across all districts and five major rallies. It also called for future elections to be conducted using ballot papers and urged the Supreme Court to expedite cases concerning the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) and alleged electoral “malpractices”.At a meeting attended by leaders of 19 political parties, the opposition grouping decided that all its MPs would march to the Election Commission on October 6, while its leaders would meet the President to raise concerns over alleged irregularities in voter-list revisions.The opposition bloc also discussed demanding the Chief Election Commissioner’s resignation and declared that it would not relent until he was removed from office.
Article Summary: Congress MP Jairam Ramesh also questioned the "intentions" of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar. The Congress-led opposition INDIA bloc on Wednesday announced joint “Save Democracy” marches across all districts and five major rallies.

Article Title: Multiple Indian payloads reach orbit aboard SpaceX’s Falcon 9
Article Text:
SpaceX Falcon 9 launches multiple Indian payloads into orbit (representational image)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

BENGALURU: Multiple Indian payloads, representing four space startups, reached orbit aboard SpaceX’s Falcon 9 rocket, which lifted off at 12:02 am IST on Friday (October 2) as part of the Transporter-18 rideshare mission.The mission carried satellites developed by Dhruva Space and TakeMe2Space, along with payloads from SatLeo Labs and EON Space Labs. The payloads will demonstrate technologies for thermal imaging, Earth observation and artificial intelligence (AI)-based data processing in orbit.Dhruva’s LEAP-2 satellite, its second commercial mission using the P-30 satellite platform, was successfully deployed into orbit at 1 am IST. It hosts two in-orbit demonstration payloads: a star tracker developed by France-based Sodern, part of ArianeGroup, and TAPAS-1, developed by SatLeo Labs.SatLeo describes TAPAS-1, or Thermal Access Platform for Analytics & Solutions, as India’s first dedicated commercial thermal payload. The CubeSat-category payload uses thermal infrared sensing to capture temperature information that conventional optical satellite imagery cannot directly provide.The mission will validate its thermal sensing technology, payload performance and data-processing capabilities in orbit.“Most satellites show us what the Earth looks like, TAPAS-1 will show us how it behaves by revealing temperature patterns that ordinary payloads cannot see,” said Shravan Bhati, co-founder and CEO, SatLeo Labs.Dhruva Space also undertook the end-to-end integration of LEAP-2 with the Falcon 9 launch vehicle. The company said this builds on its work on LEAP-1, through which it became the first Indian private company to undertake the launch vehicle integration of its satellite in-house.“This extends our role beyond satellite manufacturing into launch integration and end-to-end mission delivery, reinforcing its full-stack Space engineering approach. LEAP-2 will also be supported by our growing global ground infrastructure, including its owned and operated ground station in Luleå, Sweden; the first non-govt entity owned and operated ground station outside India, authorised by the GoI to provide Ground-Station-as-a-Service,” the firm added.TakeMe2Space’s 14-kg MOI-1A satellite is designed to allow customers to run AI models on Earth-observation data directly in orbit. It carries onboard computing capacity of 117 trillion operations per second (TOPS), 2 TB of storage and a nine-band multispectral imager. Processing imagery in space could reduce the need to transmit large volumes of raw data to Earth, with potential applications in agriculture, mining and supply-chain intelligence.MOI-1A follows TakeMe2Space’s 2024 MOI-TD technology demonstration, which validated onboard AI inference and data processing. The company said it had signed up 23 customers for its in-orbit inference services.MOI-1A also carried MIRA, a 502-g optical telescope developed by EON Space Labs. “A compact optical telescope engineered for space imaging. It delivers high-resolution Earth observation with exceptional stability and thermal robustness,” EON describes the payload.MIRA is a pathfinder for a planned small satellite constellation. Its flight comes after the loss of the PSLV-C62 mission on Jan 12, which had affected the company’s earlier launch plans.“Satellites collect vast amounts of data, but much of it still has to reach the ground before it can be turned into useful information. With MOI-1A, customers will be able to run their AI models directly in orbit and receive the insights they need, without downloading all the raw imagery. This mission is an important step towards making computing in space a service that businesses can use,” Ronak Kumar Samantray, founder and CEO, TakeMe2Space, said.
Article Summary: Multiple Indian payloads, representing four space startups, reached orbit aboard SpaceX’s Falcon 9 rocket. The mission carried satellites developed by Dhruva Space and TakeMe2Space, along with payloads from SatLeo Labs and EON Space Labs. The payloads will demonstrate technologies for thermal imaging, Earth observation and artificial intelligence-based data processing in orbit.

Article Title: Supreme Court refuses to de-freeze TMC accounts, says let Calcutta high court decide
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Thursday rejected a petition by Mamata Banerjee-headed TMC faction seeking de-freezing of its three bank accounts on grounds that the party required funds to carry out political activities, such as holding rallies and meetings.Challenging Calcutta HC's order allowing only meeting of day-to-day expenses of the party from these accounts, senior advocate A M Singhvi said the party's three Indian Bank accounts, which have been given a clean chit by the Enforcement Directorate (ED) in a separate proceeding, should be allowed to be operated by the party.Solicitor general Tushar Mehta, appearing for West Bengal govt, told a bench of Justices M M Sundresh and P B Varale that the accounts in question are frozen based on the FIR lodged by the state police, as there is evidence that Rs 35 crore, generated from the fraudulent sale of government land after it was misrepresented as private land by Abhishek Banerjee's PS Sumit Roy, was deposited in these bank accounts.Mehta also mentioned there is a plea pending before the EC as to which is the real TMC, the faction headed by Mamata or the rival group, adding that the EC has frozen the party symbol and allotted both factions ad hoc symbols to contest bypolls.The bench said it would not examine merits of the case as it is l pending with HC, which in the interim has already rejected the plea for de-freezing the accounts. It requested the HC to expedite adjudication of the pending petition on the issue.In its petition, the Mamata faction said it urgently required funds to meet expenses that would arise from preparations for the bypolls.Referring to an earlier ED proceeding freezing its three HDFC bank accounts, TMC said, "The FIR does not pertain to its Indian Bank accounts as no transaction is linked to the four bank accounts to the alleged offence.Successive and progressive freezing of TMC's bank accounts indicates mala fide use of power by state authorities to paralyse operations of a nationally recognised party."
Article Summary: Supreme Court rejects petition by Mamata Banerjee-headed TMC faction seeking de- freezing of its three bank accounts. In its petition, the Mamata faction said it urgently required funds to meet expenses that would arise from preparations for bypolls.

Article Title: PFRDA eyes plan for funds to invest directly in infrastructure
Article Text:
PFRDA expects 2-3 crore new NPS subscribers over next two years

NEW DELHI: The Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA) is preparing a roadmap to allow entities regulated by it to invest directly in large infrastructure projects, beyond the current mechanism of investing through ReITS, InVITS and alternate investment funds (AIFs), chairman S Raman told TOI."A committee has been set up to look at the issue, and internal discussions are under way to evolve a mechanism where PFRDA can invest directly in such projects. It will be long, patient capital and may be possible at least five years down the line," said Raman on the sidelines of an event on NPS Diwas.Globally, Canadian pension funds are known to invest directly in big infra projects, including in India, and they hold a significant stake in such projects, including through equity. "All such modalities are being looked into," said Raman.At the event, financial services secretary Sanjay Lohiya said that as the domestic "pension kitty" grows, people are hopeful that a lot of long-term investment, particularly in infrastructure, will be provided by these pension funds."Risk, reward and the quality of investment have to be kept in mind, but govt and other stakeholders are hopeful that slowly our pension funds will be able to provide patient capital."The officer also said that despite the government introducing the Unified Pension Scheme (UPS), which provides an assured and inflation-indexed monthly pension equivalent to 50% of the average basic pay drawn in the last 12 months, most employees covered under NPS "choose" not to opt for the scheme.Raman also said that PFRDA is stepping up efforts to expand NPS beyond govt employees and the corporate sector, with focus on informal workers, self-employed people and small business owners. "PFRDA aims to add two to three crore subscribers to the NPS in the next two years."
Article Summary: Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA) is preparing a roadmap to allow entities regulated by it to invest directly in large infrastructure projects. PFRDA expects 2-3 crore new NPS subscribers over next two years. Canadian pension funds are known to investment directly in big infra projects, including in India.

NEW DELHI: The CBI on Thursday filed its second chargesheet in the Rs 7,429-crore Reliance Home Finance Ltd (RHFL) alleged loan diversion case, naming 11 accused, including three senior executives of the Reliance ADA Group and seven corporate entities.The chargesheet alleges criminal conspiracy and cheating that led to massive wrongful losses for a consortium of public sector banks and financial institutions.Among the individuals charged are RHFL director and chief financial officer Amit Bapna, Reliance Capital Group MD and vice chairperson Amitabh Jhunjhunwala, Reliance Power CFO Suresh Nagarajan, and RHFL's statutory auditor Vijay Napawaliya.The seven companies named as accused include Reliance Infrastructure, Reliance Power, Reliance Big Entertainment, Reliance Broadcast Network, Reliance Business Broadcast News Holdings, Reliance MediaWorks Financial Services, and Kunjbihari Developers.According to the probe agency, RHFL borrowed funds from lending institutions and allegedly siphoned off Rs 7,429 crore through a web of intermediary and conduit entities.These funds were ultimately diverted to various Reliance ADA Group companies in direct violation of lending terms, causing substantial financial harm to the banks while wrongfully enriching the accused individuals and related companies.The investigation stems from complaints initially filed by the Union Bank of India and other public sector bank consortium members.This latest filing brings the total number of accused charged in the specific RHFL case to 15, following an initial chargesheet filed against four individuals on July 9. Article Title: Govt backs SCO connectivity, trade agenda but PM’s Pak visit uncertain

NEW DELHI: India’s participation in the SCO meeting of national coordinators in Islamabad to firm up the calendar for high-level meetings has sparked speculation about whether PM Narendra Modi would travel to Pakistan for the heads of state summit next year. Modi has missed only 1 of the 7 in-person summits since India became a full member of the Eurasian bloc in 2017 but Indian officials warn his past attendance is no guarantee of a visit even for a multilateral event to Pakistan, a country India has come to describe as a serial practitioner of terrorism.A senior Indian diplomat, Alok Dimri, travelled to Pakistan this week for the national coordinators’ meeting, as first reported by TOI on Monday. The first such visit from India to Pakistan since the Pahalgam terrorist attack highlighted how the SCO, which is dominated by China and Russia, has remained insulated from India-Pakistan tensions, unlike the more modest SAARC regional framework.For a PM visit though, as official sources said, India will factor in Pakistan’s continued support for cross-border terrorism before making a final decision. The same is likely to apply for the meetings of defence and foreign ministers heading into the main summit, as India seeks tangible and irreversible action by Pakistan against cross-border terrorism to make the overall environment conducive for any substantive engagement.After the meeting this week, Pakistan PM Shehbaz Sharif will soon write to leaders of all member-states inviting them for the SCO heads of state summit. He had last invited Modi for the heads of government meeting in Islamabad in 2024 but India had then sent external affairs minister S Jaishankar who usually represents India in that meeting.Modi attends the meetings of the Council of Heads of State (CHS), the supreme decision-making body of the SCO which meets annually on a rotational basis in the country chairing the SCO. Pakistan assumed the chairship from Kyrgyzstan at the Bishkek summit last month.Although Modi did skip the Kazakhstan summit in 2024, India will likely weigh multiple geopolitical factors before deciding on his potential visit to Pakistan, apart from Pakistan-backed terrorism. India’s engagement with the SCO facilitates the ongoing normalisation of relations with China while preserving its strategic and longstanding ties with Russia.Ironically, counterterrorism and security cooperation is one key reason for New Delhi’s engagements with the grouping that also helps India with Central Asian connectivity and regional security in Afghanistan, while reinforcing its strategic autonomy.Additional secretary Dimri was greeted warmly in Pakistan, with an official photo showing him standing next to Pakistan deputy PM and foreign minister Ishaq Dar. Dimri said the national coordinators had finalised an agenda for common wellbeing and prosperity with focus on connectivity, trade and transit. “This programme will continue for a year and will culminate with Islamabad Summit,” he said.

Article Title: Supreme Court says seize vehicle, stop RC, PUC renewal if e-challans not paid
Article Text:
SC said cops could issue lakhs of e-challans, but what was being done to recover the fines was the question at hand.

NEW DELHI: Many vehicle owners often ignore traffic fines for years, allowing unpaid challans to pile up and eventually land in courts. Supreme Court has now directed states and UTs to impound their vehicles, noting that around 47% of challans issued across the country remain unpaid.A bench of Justices JB Pardiwala and KV Viswanathan said Thursday that issuing e-challans was not sufficient and stringent action should be taken to recover fines."Let there be random checking of vehicles, and if it is found that the e-challan issued has not been abided by or honoured, necessary steps shall be taken to impound the vehicle itself," the bench said.SC said the authorities should freeze online services for vehicles with outstanding amounts. They should bar renewal of registration certificates, issuing of duplicate registration certificates, and not entertain any request to update the owner's address, it said. "The authorities shall also deny fitness certificate until all pending traffic fines are entirely cleared and further there should be blacklisting of the vehicle concerned on the Parivahan portal," SC said."This will come in the way of the person concerned if he wants to sell his vehicle.The authorities should also proceed to block ownership transfer. For multiple violations, driving licence shall be suspended from renewal, and measures shall also be taken to suspend the driving licence which may be in force. What is most important is that no centre should be permitted to issue a PUC certificate," the bench said.Expressing displeasure with authorities for not taking action, the bench said, "We want to convey something to states/UTs/authorities plainly and simply. It is not sufficient to keep issuing e-challans to the person who is alleged to have violated the provisions of the law."SC said cops could issue lakhs of e-challans, but what was being done to recover the fines was the question at hand."We are informed by the amicus... that states/UTs have to recover Rs 49,194 crore approximately towards the e-challans issued over a period of time. We are also informed that so far an amount of Rs 26,175 crore has been recovered.What we want to convey in simple words is that authorities need to work at the ground level, having regard to the ground realities," the bench said.With the case being heard for over a decade, the court decided to check the ground situation regarding implementation of its orders."We have been monitoring this litigation by now over a period of almost 14 years. This writ petition is of 2012... During this interregnum period of one year, we have issued a slew of directions for meaningful and effective implementation of various provisions of Motor Vehicles Act and Central Motor Vehicles Rules framed therein," it said, adding that if all these were going to remain on paper and not going to be implemented, then "we may have to take stern action which may not be liked by the authorities".
Article Summary: Supreme Court has now directed states and UTs to impound their vehicles. Justices JB Pardiwala and KV Viswanathan said Thursday that issuing e-challans was not sufficient. Around 47% of challans issued across the country remain unpaid.

Article Title: 'Right to access to justice equal for all': SC frowns at out-of-turn hearings
Article Text:
'When we grant early hearing to one litigant who has the resources to approach the SC, we do injustice to millions of litigants who are waiting for a hearing on their petitions,' the bench said.

Sacked for taking bribe, can’t allow early hearing: SC

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court on Thursday said a bus conductor's right to access to justice is equal to that of a top bureaucrat, and granting out-of-turn hearing to a litigant having the wherewithal to approach the SC would violate the right to speedy justice of millions languishing in the queue.A bench of Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana refused to entertain a plea for expeditious hearing of a petition by an additional district judge challenging his dismissal from service for corruption in 2022. His petition has been pending in Allahabad HC since 2022."When we grant early hearing to one litigant who has the resources to approach the SC, we do injustice to millions of litigants who are waiting for a hearing on their petitions," the bench said.In his plea for a direction to HC for expeditious disposal of his plea, the judge said he has suffered a lot in the last four years and that since his retirement is due on Nov 30, he would like to leave service with dignity.Referring to the pendency of more than 12 lakh cases in Allahabad HC, the bench told the counsel: "You are making a submission which is against the equal right to access to justice of every litigant, be it a bus conductor or a principal secretary.We will not request HC to grant out-of-turn hearing unless we are convinced about egregious circumstances in the case that warrant urgent hearing."The petitioner is one of the three additional district judges - Ashok Kumar Singh, Himanshu Bhatnagar and Rakesh Kumar Nain - who were dismissed from service on corruption charges through a full court resolution passed by Allahabad HC in May 2022.He complained that "no show-cause notice was ever issued to the petitioner and no opportunity was ever afforded to give any representation against the major penalty so imposed upon the petitioner, therefore, the resolution dated May 12, 2022, and the order dated May 17, 2022, by which the services of the petitioner were terminated, was passed in violation of principles of natural justice".The bench said that as the petitioner has been dismissed from service on charges of acceptance of bribe, it is not a fit case for requesting the HC to grant an out-of-turn hearing.The petitioner, who joined judicial service in Aug 1999 and was promoted as additional district judge in 2013, was accused of taking a Rs 6 lakh bribe to acquit a person in 2015. The inquiry and disciplinary proceedings were concluded in 2022, following which his services were terminated.
Article Summary: A bench of Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana refused to entertain a plea for expeditious hearing of a petition by an additional district judge challenging his dismissal from service for corruption in 2022. The bench said that as the petitioner has been dismissed from service on charges of acceptance of bribe, it is not a fit case for requesting the HC to grant an out-of-turn hearing.

NEW DELHI: AIMIM chief Asaduddin Owaisi on Thursday said his party was open to forming an electoral alliance with other political parties in Uttar Pradesh ahead of next year’s Assembly elections, saying it did not want the BJP to return to power in the state for a third consecutive term.Addressing a press conference, Owaisi said AIMIM would contest the elections “with all our force” and would announce any alliance once it was finalised.“We don't want the BJP to come to power in Uttar Pradesh for the third time. In order to stop this from happening, we are open for alliance. What else can we say?” Owaisi said, according to new agency PTI.He referred to AIMIM’s experience in Bihar, where four of the party’s five MLAs joined the RJD in June 2022. The move enabled the RJD to reclaim its position as the single largest party in the Bihar Assembly.Owaisi said AIMIM had sought only six seats in Bihar previously and alleged that its concerns had not received the same political attention as similar developments involving other parties.“We fought again and people voted for us. We bagged five seats there,” he said.“It is up to them (political parties in UP) now. We will contest the elections there with all our force, and whenever an alliance happens, we will let you know.We will decide our fate and make our leadership,” Owaisi added.The Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections are scheduled to be held early next year to elect all 403 members of the House.Owaisi also criticised political parties that have attributed electoral defeats both to AIMIM’s presence in contests and to alleged vote theft.“The opposition once said that they lost the elections because we (AIMIM) were in the fray. Sometimes, they say that they lost the elections because of vote theft. How is this possible? They should be clear,” he said.Owaisi also criticised the implementation of the Uniform Civil Code (UCC) in some states and alleged that the move was aimed at turning India into a “Hindu Rashtra”.He claimed that the UCC laws in Uttarakhand, Assam and Gujarat were a “cut and paste” of the Hindu Marriage Act and Hindu Succession Act, and questioned their applicability to Muslims.“The Maharashtra government is working on UCC now. But the laws in Uttarakhand, Assam and Gujarat are the same. It is just a 'cut and paste' of Hindu Marriage Act and Hindu Succession Act,” Owaisi said.He said tribals had been excluded from the UCC in Uttarakhand and Gujarat because of differences in their religious and social practices, and argued that Muslims faced a similar issue.“When marriage in Islam is a contract and it is a bond for life time, how can Hindu Marriage Act be imposed on me? Why should I marry according to it?” he asked.Owaisi further alleged that UCC provisions could affect inheritance arrangements and said the move violated Articles 25, 26 and 29 of the Constitution.“BJP leaders say that women should get equal share (in property). In Assam, Uttarakhand and Gujarat where UCC was implemented, the power of will helps a person give away (the property) to just one son when he has three. UCC is an effort to implement the laws of Hindus over Muslims. This is a violation of Article 25, 26 and 29 (of the Indian Constitution). It is a way to make India a Hindu Rashtra,” he said.
Article Summary: AIMIM chief Asaduddin Owaisi says his party is open to forming an electoral alliance with other political parties in Uttar Pradesh ahead of next year’s Assembly elections. Article Title: Full-body scanners at airports: Govt tests tech & algorithms to address privacy concerns before wider rollout

NEW DELHI: India's aviation security regulator is collecting data from ongoing trials of full-body scanners at Bengaluru and Cochin airports before deciding on their wider deployment, with the technology's algorithms also being refined to account for objects commonly worn by passengers in India.Bureau of Civil Aviation Security (BCAS) Director General Rajesh Nirwan told reporters on Thursday that full-body scanners have been mandated at eight airports, while trials are currently being conducted at Bengaluru and Cochin. Authorities are collecting data from the trials, including the number of alarms generated, which will be assessed before a decision is taken on introducing the scanners at airports.However, Cochin is not among the eight airports where the scanners have been mandated.The deployment of full-body scanners has been delayed for years, partly due to concerns over passenger privacy. Nirwan said newer scanners are being made “image agnostic”, meaning they do not produce an actual image of the passenger but instead display a model and identify the specific part of the body where a suspicious object may have been detected, reported PTI.BCAS is also working with scanner vendors and original equipment manufacturers to refine the technology for Indian conditions, including concerns that jewellery and other commonly worn items could trigger alarms.“What we are getting today in India is based on algorithms that have been designed for foreign markets. There are certain typical things that are on the body of Indian citizens or people living in India. So, those algorithms are also being continuously refined,” Nirwan said.The data collected during the ongoing trials will be used to further refine the algorithms, he added.Meanwhile, the officials also addressed the recent Flydubai cockpit attack in which Indian pilot Smit Machchhar was injured, saying Indian aviation authorities are examining the incident and will hold internal deliberations on whether any aviation security advisory is required.Civil Aviation Secretary Samir Kumar Sinha said the matter was under examination and any decision on an advisory would be taken after internal discussions. “... in case some advisory is to be issued, obviously we will put it up to the higher authorities for taking a decision on that,” Sinha said.The comments came a day after Flydubai flight FZ1073, flying from Dubai to Tel Aviv with 174 passengers, was diverted to Saudi Arabia after an altercation in the cockpit. Indian captain Smit Machchhar was seriously injured while trying to tackle his co-pilot, and the aircraft later landed safely at Tabuk.
Article Summary: Full-body scanners have been mandated at eight airports, while trials are currently being conducted at Bengaluru and Cochin. Authorities are collecting data from the trials, including the number of alarms generated, which will be assessed before a decision is taken on introducing the scanners at airports.

Article Title: PM Modi urges UPSC to test aspirants’ motivation for joining civil services, not just academic knowledge
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Emphasising that the purpose of recruitment for govt jobs should be to bring people into public service rather than public office, Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Thursday asked recruitment agencies like Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) to adopt selection parameters that not only test an aspirant's academic knowledge but also their motivation to join the civil services.Modi, while addressing UPSC's centenary celebrations here, explained that selecting individuals with the right inherent motivation makes it easier for the administration to adapt to rapidly changing public aspirations. Stating that the youths recruited today will simultaneously serve as the chief architects and the primary beneficiaries of the nation's future, he insisted that every selection process be rigorously tested against the dual criteria of prioritizing the nation and the citizen.Modi said the archaic 'mai-baap' (supremacy) governance mindset of the past has made way for a modern administrative era built on the absolute principle of 'nagrik devo bhava' or 'citizen is king". Projecting India as an increasingly urbanized nation by 2047 with a narrowing rural-urban divide, he said the traditional service delivery models will need to evolve to match the speed of an instant-delivery world where citizens demand rapid, real-time solutions powered by AI.“This changing mindset demands new changes from our civil services as well,” noted Modi.He demanded that selection processes for govt jobs at both national and state levels be meticulously designed to recruit professionals who proactively anticipate problems and operate without unnecessary pressure or influence. He emphasized the need for empathetic civil servants who find innovative solutions, proactively ease citizens' lives, and critically evaluate the impact of laws on the public.Cautioning the future civil servants about having to navigate new-age threats like information warfare, deepfakes, algorithmic bias, and climate justice, the prime minister instructed the recruitment agencies to adapt to these global shifts by prioritizing candidates' foresight and complex problem-solving abilities.He insisted that the examination agencies rapidly align with the nation's broader reform momentum by adopting the principle of time certainty to shorten exam cycles without lowering standards. These would cut down the financial burden on account of coaching fees, rent, and transport, on the families, he said.The prime minister proudly noted the dramatic rise in female candidates in civil services, from a mere 3% in 1952 to over 30%today, alongside the historic appointment of three out of four women UPSC chairpersons post-2014.Pointing to the 45-fold increase in candidate participation since the institution's 50th anniversary in 1976, Modi reminded the commissions that the recruiting agencies are not merely picking candidates, but choosing individuals who will become the very face and representative of the government at the grassroots level.Congratulating UPSC for having been in existence for 100 years, the prime minister praised the organisation's enduring credibility despite changing generations, governments, technologies, and syllabi. The celebrations were marked by the release of a commemorative postage stamp, a special coin, and a compilation of 100 significant case laws.Recalling the monumental challenges faced after independence, Modi paid deep homage to Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel for establishing the vital steel frame required not just to keep the country independent, but to actively govern the newly formed nation. He acknowledged that while the UPSC has excellently discharged its historical duties, the focus must now decisively pivot toward the critical next 25 years that await the country.
Article Summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi asked recruitment agencies like Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) to adopt selection parameters that not only test an aspirant's academic knowledge but also their motivation to join the civil services.Modi, while addressing UPSC's centenary celebrations here, explained that selecting individuals with the right inherent motivation makes it easier for the administration to adapt to rapidly changing public aspirations.

Article Title: New liquor shops in Bengal must maintain 500-metre gap from schools, religious places
Article Text:
In a bid to regulate the liquor trade, the West Bengal government has raised the distance criteria for new liquor outlets from educational institutions and places of worship.

The West Bengal government has increased the necessary distance for new retail liquor outlets from educational institutions and holy places to 500 meters in urban and municipal areas and 1 km in other parts of the state, up from the former 300 meters, as per PTI.As per the recent notification given by the government, no new liquor licenses would be given within a 1 km distance of religious institutions, schools, and universities in rural and non-municipal areas, state Liquor Association Secretary Bijan Patra stated on Thursday.The government has kept the minimum distance at 500 meters from the religious places, schools, and educational insititutions for the areas under the Kolkata Municipal corporation (KMC) and other civic authorities, Bijan Patra added.However, he stated that Rule 8's distance requirements won't apply if an existing liquor store wishes to "shift" to a mall of any size.The prior framework required a minimum distance of 1,000 feet, or around 300 meters.Chief minister Suvendu Adhikari had already announced that his administration will not enable liquor sales within a 1 km radius of schools, universities, and shrines.Over 4,000 bars, off-shops, and liquor stores now operate within a 1-kilometer radius of these sensitive zones throughout the state; however, this new restriction will not affect already-existing establishments.In order to establish new offshops through bars, the new strategy also makes use of Section 4P of the excise act.However, some business owners have voiced reservations about the provision, claiming that because the state agency would keep a profit, it could not be advantageous for the liquor sector.
Article Summary: The West Bengal government has increased the necessary distance for new retail liquor outlets from educational institutions and holy places to 500 meters in urban and municipal areas and 1 km in other parts of the state. Article Title: 'Show me one damaged vehicle': Nitin Gadkari's dare on ethanol blending, targets vested interests
Article Text:
Gadkari addressing Rising Bihar Investor Summit 2026

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Union minister Nitin Gadkari on Thursday talked about the Centre's ethanol-blending programme, rejecting claims that mixing ethanol with petrol damages vehicles and arguing that the policy has also opened a new avenue for farmers to diversify beyond food production.Speaking at the inaugural session of the Bihar Investor Summit 2026, Gadkari said millions of vehicles had already been operating on ethanol-blended petrol since 2022 without, in his account, widespread complaints of damage."I challenge anybody to come up with the complaint that his or her vehicle has suffered damage on this account. Of course, those with vested interests may have some other story to tell," said Gadkari, who holds portfolios of Road Transport and Highways, as quoted by PTI.Gadkari said the policy was designed not merely to reduce dependence on conventional fuel but also to create an additional market for agricultural produce. "We must understand that the decision to blend ethanol with petrol was taken with a view to diversification of agriculture towards energy and power sectors... Our farmers shall no longer remain 'anna data' (food producers) but also become 'urja data' (energy producers)," he said.According to Gadkari, about 4 crore four-wheelers and 20 crore two-wheelers have been running on petrol blended with ethanol since 2022. He also claimed that major automobile manufacturers had tested vehicles using higher ethanol blends, including 100% ethanol."Of course, we are importing (conventional fuel) worth Rs 22 lakh crore, and those who feel that their business will get hit are bound to feel bad. But let me tell you, I am the minister in charge of the department concerned; all leading automobile brands have tried running their vehicles even on 100 per cent ethanol. And there have been no complaints," he said.The minister also linked ethanol production to higher farm incomes, saying the use of corn for ethanol had generated additional earnings for farmers in Bihar and Uttar Pradesh."After the Union government took the decision to make ethanol out of corn and the same was used for the aforementioned purposes, it resulted in additional earnings of up to Rs 45,000 crore for farmers of Bihar and Uttar Pradesh. Is it not preferable to serve the interests of those from whom we import (fuel)," he asked.Gadkari cited other examples of efforts to develop alternative fuels, including aviation fuel made using agricultural waste. "We have even made aviation fuel with rice straw. The future belongs to innovation, technology and research. And a state like Bihar has to play a key role in this direction," he said.Turning to Bihar's investment potential, Gadkari said the state could expand its economic base through sectors such as tourism. He also pointed to international demand for makhana, a crop widely produced in the state.He described Bihar as having significant economic potential and praised Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary's leadership."Under the leadership of Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary, the state is bound to scale new heights," he said.Meanwhile, Choudhary, addressing the summit, appealed to investors to set up businesses in Bihar and assured them of access to a large market if their products met the required standards.
Article Summary: Gadkari: Millions of vehicles have already been operating on ethanol-blended petrol since 2022. He said the policy was designed not merely to reduce dependence on conventional fuel but also to create an additional market for agricultural produce. Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary appealed to investors to set up businesses in Bihar.

Article Title: Himachal implements mandatory dress code for teachers in government CBSE schools

Himachal Pradesh implemented a mandatory dress code for teachers across 148 government CBSE schools on Thursday, attempting to create a more organised and professional learning environment.A notice dated September 10 explained that the prescribed dress code has been formulated "keeping in view the professional requirements of the teaching profession, uniformity in appearance and the climatic conditions of Himachal Pradesh."The dress code's colour palette includes light lilac, lilac purple and navy blue, with black prescribed for footwear and other specified accessories.The prescribed dress code offers female teachers three alternatives: a saree with a blazer, a kurta/kameez with pants, a plazo or salwar and a blazer, and a shirt and blazer with pants and a tie. Article Title: Watch: Tamil Nadu CM Vijay launches one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns
Article Text:
Vijay presented 22-carat, one-gram gold rings to 25 newborns. (PTI)

Who is eligible for the gold ring?

Scheme draws on Tamil tradition

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Monday rolled out the state government’s one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns in Madurai. He also held some of the newborns and presented the rings to beneficiaries during the launch programme.Under the scheme, eligible babies born in government hospitals and government primary health centres will receive a 22-carat, one-gram gold ring.The initiative, named the Maternal Uncle Gold Ring Scheme (Thaaimaman Thanga Mothiram Thittam), has an annual allocation of Rs 755.83 crore.It is aimed at celebrating motherhood, promoting maternal and child health and encouraging institutional deliveries by increasing public confidence in government healthcare facilities.The scheme will cover babies born on or after June 22, 2026, to mothers who are permanent residents of Tamil Nadu and have delivered at government healthcare institutions.Mothers must be registered under the Pregnancy and Infant Cohort Monitoring and Evaluation (PICME) system and have a Reproductive and Child Health (RCH) ID. They will also have to provide an e-KYC-verified Aadhaar card along with one of the prescribed identity or residence documents.These include ration cards, voter identity cards, Labour Welfare Board identity cards, Department of Posts address cards and nativity certificates.The state government has already procured 1.28 lakh one-gram gold rings for the initial rollout. Each ring will have a unique serial number and will be packed in tamper-proof packaging.From Monday, babies born in government hospitals will receive the rings at the time of discharge, according to the state government.To clear the backlog of eligible babies born between June 22 and Monday, the government will distribute the rings through 107 hubs across Tamil Nadu.Distribution will begin at the rate of 100 babies per day at each hub. At designated centres, 25 beneficiaries will be accommodated in the morning and another 25 in the afternoon to avoid overcrowding, PTI reported.Village Health Nurses will distribute invitations informing beneficiaries of their allotted date and time. Beneficiaries have been asked to visit the designated centres only at the time mentioned in their invitations.The district administration has also made transportation arrangements for beneficiaries from their respective areas. Vijay had announced the scheme ahead of the April 23 Assembly election as a symbolic gift to newborns, drawing on the Tamil tradition of ‘Thaimaaman Seer’. The scheme has retrospective effect from June 22, Vijay’s birthday.A government order issued on June 23 described the initiative as a token celebrating the birth of a child, motherhood and the cultural tradition of ‘Thaimaaman’.According to ANI, Tamil Nadu minister Arun Raj explained the cultural significance of the initiative saying, "A maternal uncle is someone who is among the first to rush in when a child is born, sharing in his sister’s happiness as his own. He assures her that he will always stand by her and her child, offering love, support and a sense of security.""Today, the Tamil Nadu Government, under the leadership of our brother, Mr. Vijay, is embracing this sacred bond of the maternal uncle and, as a gesture of that affection, is set to provide a one-gram gold ring to every child born in government hospitals. When the scheme was announced and the question arose as to where it should be launched, the place chosen by our Chief Minister was Madurai. This is the sacred soil of Madurai, blessed with the compassion and grace of Mother Meenakshi," he added.Tamil Nadu records around 7.8 lakh deliveries annually, with institutional deliveries accounting for 99.9% of births, according to NFHS-6. Government health facilities account for nearly 4.2 lakh deliveries, or around 53% of the total.According to the state government, the average out-of-pocket expenditure for a delivery at a government hospital is Rs 1,364, compared with Rs 63,473 at a private hospital.The government said the scheme is intended to encourage safe institutional deliveries, strengthen maternal and child welfare and increase public trust in government healthcare services.The Tamil Nadu Medical Services Corporation will procure the gold rings based on annual requirements, while a project and programme management unit will oversee implementation and monitoring.
Article Summary: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Monday rolled out the state government’s one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns in Madurai. The scheme will cover babies born on or after June 22, 2026, to mothers who are permanent residents of Tamil Nadu and have delivered at government healthcare institutions. Vijay had announced the scheme ahead of the April 23 Assembly election.

Article Title: Brij Bhushan acquittal challenged over ‘stereotypical assumptions’ about sexual assault victims
Article Text:
Wrestlers challenge acquittal, cite ‘stereotypical assumptions’

NEW DELHI: The Rouse Avenue court has issued notice to former Wrestling Federation of India (WFI) chief Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh and others on an appeal challenging his acquittal in a sexual harassment case involving women wrestlers.Special Judge Dig Vinay Singh sought a response to the appeal and listed the matter for hearing on October 9. The court also directed that the original affidavit and orders containing the names of the victims be placed in a sealed envelope. It further directed the appellant to file a copy of the petition with the victims’ names redacted.The appeal challenges the August 3 order of the Rouse Avenue court, Brij Bhushan and Vinod Tomar in the case. The wrestlers have contended that the acquittal order is unsustainable in law and is based on a “manifestly erroneous and selective appreciation of the evidence on record”.The appeal has contended that the impugned order proceeds on conjectures and surmises, fails to apply binding and well-settled principles of law, and, in material part, rests its reasoning on “archaic and stereotypical assumptions” about the “expected” behaviour of victims of sexual assault and harassment, rather than on a fair, evidence-based assessment after taking into account the circumstances of the victims.The case stems from an FIR filed by Delhi Police following a complaint by a woman wrestler during Singh’s tenure as WFI chief. The police had invoked Sections 354, 354-D, 354-A, 506(1) and 109 of the Indian Penal Code.Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate Ashwani Panwar had acquitted Singh and Tomar after a trial that was conducted in a closed courtroom. The two were tried in connection with allegations of sexual harassment of women wrestlers in India and abroad.Delhi Police had filed a 1,500-page charge sheet against Singh and Tomar on June 15, 2023, following its investigation into the allegations.The women wrestlers had earlier staged a protest at Jantar Mantar, following which the FIR was registered by Delhi Police based on the complaint.Advocate Rajiv Mohan, assisted by Rehan Khan and Rishabh Bhati, represented Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh, while senior advocate Rebecca John appeared for the victims and complainants.
Article Summary: The appeal challenges the August 3 order of the Rouse Avenue court, Brij Bhushan and Vinod Tomar in the case. The wrestlers have contended that the acquittal order is unsustainable in law and is based on a “manifestly erroneous and selective appreciation of the evidence on record”

NEW DELHI: The Congress on Monday questioned Prime Minister Narendra Modi for not addressing rising inflation in his Mann Ki Baat radio address, accusing him of being “blissfully unconcerned” about the issue.The opposition party’s attack came a day after PM Modi addressed the nation in the 138th episode of Mann Ki Baat.“The brunt of inflation is no longer confined just to the kitchen, yet the Prime Minister remains blissfully unconcerned, beating his drum away. In such a scenario, how is the common family supposed to meet its needs?” Congress MP Jairam Ramesh wrote on X.Ramesh questioned why PM Modi continues to “sermonise” in the Mann Ki Baat series instead of addressing the public’s concerns.“In his ‘Mann Ki Baat’ radio series, the Prime Minister keeps sermonising on various issues, but when will he address the country’s most pressing concern—inflation? The public is already beleaguered by rising prices, and there’s no relief coming from the government.How on earth is the average family supposed to manage its budget? How long will the middle class and the poor have their backs broken like this?” the Rajya Sabha MP asked.According to the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation’s (MoSPI) Consumer Price Index (CPI) release, retail inflation, based on the 2024=100 CPI, stood at 4.82% in August, up from 4.45% in July. Food inflation, measured by the Consumer Food Price Index (CFPI), rose to 5.95% in August from 5.52% in July. Ginger recorded inflation of 73.82%, while garlic inflation stood at 43.60%. In contrast, tomato prices fell 31.09% year-on-year, while potato prices declined 13.14%.MoSPI data showed inflation in the combined food and beverages category at 5.66% in August. Transport inflation stood at 4.60 percent, education services at 3.73%, while restaurants and accommodation services recorded inflation of 8.38%. Personal care, social protection and miscellaneous goods and services registered inflation of 15.17%.The CPI data was compiled from price information collected across 1,407 urban markets, including online markets, and 1,465 villages nationwide. MoSPI reported a 100% response rate from both rural and urban markets in August.According to MoSPI, the next CPI data, covering September, is scheduled to be released on October 12.

Article Title: Lung cancer deaths down 16% with low-dose CT screening: IARC
Article Text:
Lung cancer deaths can be reduced through low-dose CT screening, which can also help detect the disease before it reaches advanced stages in people at high risk, according to an IARC assessment.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Low-dose computed tomography (CT) screening can cut the risk of dying from lung cancer by 16% in high-risk people, while also reducing the incidence of advanced stage III or IV disease, an International Agency for Research on Cancer (IARC) working group has found.Published in The New England Journal of Medicine, the assessment found established evidence that low-dose CT reduces lung cancer mortality when used in people at high risk based mainly on age and smoking history.IARC convened a working group of 23 clinicians and scientists from 17 countries, including Dr Abhishek Shankar of All India Institute of Medical Sciences, New Delhi, to assess the benefits and harms of lung cancer screening.The evidence mainly applies to people aged 50 to 80 with a substantial smoking history, typically at least 20 to 30 pack-years. Studies involving former smokers generally included those who had quit within the previous 10 to 15 years, with screening usually performed annually.In India, people aged 50 to 80 with at least 20 pack-years of smoking who are current smokers or quit within the past 15 years can contact the Indian Lung Screening Trial, led by Dr Abhishek Shankar at AIIMS, New Delhi, about screening.Dr Shankar has invited eligible people to contact him for screening under the trial.The evidence behind the finding came mainly from randomised trials. In the US National Lung Screening Trial, people screened with low-dose CT had a 16% lower relative risk of dying from lung cancer than those screened with chest X-rays at seven years. The European NELSON trial also found lower lung cancer mortality among men screened with low-dose CT at 10 years.Based on this evidence, the IARC group classified low-dose CT as Group A, indicating established evidence that it reduces lung cancer mortality and the incidence of stage III or IV disease. Chest X-rays, with or without sputum examination, were classified as Group C, as their ability to reduce lung cancer mortality could not be established.However, the review cautioned that low-dose CT screening is not meant for everyone. False-positive results ranged from 1% to 42% across studies, depending on the screening protocol. Among those with false-positive results, 5% to 32% underwent at least one invasive procedure, with complications occurring in 10% to 22% of such procedures.The review also estimated that 3% to 26% of lung cancers detected in randomised trials involving high-risk people could represent overdiagnosis, meaning cancers that might not have caused harm during the person's lifetime.The working group said effective lung cancer screening needs more than CT scanners, including systems for identifying eligible people, assessing risk, monitoring nodules, providing treatment and follow-up, along with smoking-cessation support. Organised programmes also require trained staff, quality assurance, adequate healthcare capacity and equitable access.
Article Summary: Low-dose computed tomography (CT) screening can cut the risk of dying from lung cancer by 16% in high-risk people. It can also reduce the incidence of advanced stage III or IV disease, according to an IARC assessment. The evidence mainly applies to people aged 50 to 80 with a substantial smoking history.

Article Title: Travis Kelce's $200 million Six Flags investment faces new low as investors push for a potential sale
Article Text:
Travis Kelce (Getty Images)

Six Flags faces mounting financial pressure

Travis Kelce’s Six Flags investment faces another test

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Six Flags is facing a fresh challenge after an investor group that includes Travis Kelce pushed the theme park company to consider a possible sale. The move comes as the operator deals with heavier losses, fewer visitors and pressure on its stock price. Jana Partners, which joined Kelce and other investors in taking a stake in Six Flags, is now seeking action from the company’s board. The development marks a sharp turn from the group’s earlier effort to help strengthen the parks and improve their appeal to families.Jana Partners reportedly contacted Six Flags’ board on Tuesday and asked it to bring in an investment bank to examine a potential sale. The request followed disappointment over the company’s latest financial results, which showed how difficult the current environment has become for the theme park operator.Six Flags posted a $203 million net loss for the second quarter, more than double the $100 million loss recorded during the same period a year earlier. Attendance also fell. The company reported 13.1 million guest visits, down about 7% from 14.2 million visits in the comparable period.The pressure has also reached the stock market. Six Flags shares traded at about $12.43 on Wednesday, roughly half their yearly peak of close to $25.Jana Partners and fellow investors, including Kelce, acquired a combined stake of around 9% in Six Flags last October. Their investment was valued at roughly $200 million at the time. Jana had previously focused on improving the company's marketing and customer experience while also considering strategic options that could increase shareholder value.Six Flags said it remains focused on its investors and its wider business plans."We have a history of engaging constructively with all of our shareholders and value their perspectives. We are focused on executing on our strategic priorities and are committed to maximizing shareholder value."Travis Kelce's connection to Six Flags goes beyond his investment. The Kansas City Chiefs star has long had an attachment to Cedar Point in Ohio, a park he visited while growing up.When the investment was announced, Kelce shared his excitement about helping shape the company's future."Couldn't pass up the opportunity to continue the tradition and make Cedar Point and Six Flags even more special for the next generation of families!"He added, "Excited to partner with JANA Partners as an investor in Six Flags. So crazy to even imagine this is real, but you gotta love it when life comes full circle."The company is also dealing with legal challenges involving its X2 roller coaster at Six Flags Magic Mountain in California. Three people who say they suffered serious brain injuries after riding the attraction have filed lawsuits. The coaster, known for rotating seats and head-first drops, remains closed.Attorney Christopher Bulone said, "No ride like that should be allowed to exist," according to CNN.Six Flags declined to comment on the pending lawsuits but confirmed to KABC that the ride "remains closed at this time."
Article Summary: Six Flags posted a $203 million net loss for the second quarter, more than double the $100 million loss recorded during the same period a year earlier. Six Flags shares traded at about $12.43 on Wednesday, roughly half their yearly peak of close to $25.
