Maria Sharapova’s financial journey didn’t end when she retired from professional tennis in 2020. The five-time Grand Slam champion had already amassed a large commercial profile during her playing career, with endorsements and business ventures supplementing her tennis earnings. Sharapova made $325 million before taxes during her career, which included endorsement income, Forbes reported.The most obvious example of her leap into entrepreneurship was her candy company, Sugarpova, which she founded in 2012. The venture gave Sharapova hands-on experience in branding, product development and business operations, and established the foundation for her later investing activities.Sharapova has built her wealth not just from professional tennis, but from a number of different income streams. Her Grand Slam wins have helped increase her global profile and partnerships with companies such as Nike, Evian, Porsche and TAG Heuer have generated significant commercial opportunities.Sugarpova was a big step in that Sharapova went from being a sponsored athlete to a business owner. The company eventually shut down, but the experience helped her develop an understanding of entrepreneurship and investment.With her tennis career, Sharapova’s commercial portfolio expanded. One of her most significant partnerships was with Nike, while brands such as Porsche, Evian and TAG Heuer helped boost her global commercial profile.Her work with Supergoop! was another on her path. Sharapova invested in and fronted the skincare company, blending her public profile with an ownership stake instead of simply using traditional endorsement deals.That meant Sharapova could learn about branding, product development and commercial strategy, all the while still capitalizing on her reputation as an elite athlete.Since retiring, Sharapova has shifted her focus more toward investment and advisory opportunities. She has worked with companies across wellness, fitness, beauty and fintech, including Therabody, Tonal, Supergoop!, Bala Bangles, Public.com and MoonPay.Her connection with Therabody was more than just a sponsorship. Sharapova became an investor and member of the company’s advisory board, bringing her professional athlete background to the wellness-focused business.She also appeared on Shark Tank and then partnered with Mark Cuban for an investment in Bala Bangles. Sharapova has also taken a seat on the board of luxury fashion group Moncler, adding corporate leadership to her entrepreneurial portfolio.These ventures mark a shift for Sharapova, from making money primarily. One of the most well-rounded athletes in the world, with a model that includes all through tennis and endorsements to a model that includes business ownership, investments and strategic advisory roles.
Article Summary: Maria Sharapova made $325 million before taxes during her career, according to Forbes. The five-time Grand Slam champion turned endorsements into long-term business opportunities. She has worked with companies across wellness, fitness, beauty and fintech. Since retiring, she has shifted her focus more toward investment and advisory opportunities.

Article Title: Why Bengaluru residents are pushing back against Airbnb-style stays in residential neighbourhoods
Article Text:
Residents said the homestay-cum-café could bring more visitors, increasing noise and disturbance in the residential area (AI Image)

Why residents are opposing the homestay

Residents seek clarity on permissions

I wanted to do this for the Gen-Z: Property owner





BENGALURU: Residents of HRBR Layout are pushing back against the proposed opening of a homestay-cum-café in their residential neighbourhood, raising concerns over noise, pollution, parking and the impact of increased commercial activity on the area.Residents of 5th A Main Road, including young and elderly residents, took to the streets with banners and slogans to oppose Blossomly House, a proposed commercial homestay-cum-cafeteria.They argued that homestay-cum-café and similar commercial facilities should not be introduced in what they described as a peaceful residential layout.The residents have also raised concerns over an alleged encroachment of a rajakaluve beside the property and the proposed installation of a commercial exhaust system.They fear the exhaust could result in considerable noise, smoke, odour and air pollution for people living in the surrounding area.Residents said the proposed homestay-cum-café could bring a steady flow of visitors into the neighbourhood, increasing noise and disturbance in an area primarily meant for residential use.“If 20–30 or more people gather and smoke at the premises, it could create significant health and nuisance concerns for neighbouring residents.Along with that, with a large number of customers entering and leaving, talking, gathering and moving around, there is a possibility of increased noise disturbance in what is otherwise a residential area,” said resident KR Prabhakar.Parking is another concern for residents, particularly those who have lived in the neighbourhood for several years. They said neighbouring roads were already experiencing commercial activity and parking pressure, and feared that the proposed establishment could further reduce parking spaces available to locals.Gomathy Venkatesan, an elderly resident, alleged that the café management did not take her objections into consideration when she initially raised them.“I have been staying here for 35 years, but when we told the owner our disagreements, he asked us to bear all the issues and stay or vacate, adding that the road will soon become a commercial hub,” she told TOI.A former leader of opposition of the erstwhile Bruhat Bengaluru Mahanagara Palike (BBMP), who joined the protest, said the area was purely residential and that no commercial development would be allowed under any circumstances.The residents have also questioned whether the proposed establishment has all the permissions required to operate in the area. They have written to Bengaluru North City Corporation (BNCC), seeking verification of permissions related to zoning, land-use compliance and rajakaluve clearance.Their concerns come as the proposed property combines a homestay with a café, bringing together accommodation and a customer-facing commercial activity within the residential layout.Sachin Jain, who owns the upcoming property, said the café was intended to “give back something to the society”. He rejected the suggestion that the project was “very commercial” and said the aim was not to cause inconvenience to residents.“I wanted to do this for the Gen-Z; this is nothing like a traditional cafe and this place will strictly be a no-smoking zone. I am also planning to incorporate a library within the place along with a homestay so that youngsters can read and take in the ambience,” Sachin said.While residents have raised concerns about the nature and impact of Airbnb-style stays and commercial activity in their neighbourhood, the property owner has maintained that the proposed facility is intended to offer a different kind of space and would not be aimed at causing inconvenience to those living nearby.
Article Summary: Residents of HRBR Layout are pushing back against the proposed opening of a homestay-cum-café in their residential neighbourhood. They have raised concerns over noise, pollution, parking and the impact of increased commercial activity on the area.

Article Title: Bengaluru-Mumbai Vande Bharat Sleeper: India's second sleeper train to start this month
Article Text:
The Indian railway board has announced the introduction of the Vande Bharat Sleeper train service





BENGALURU: After much delay, the railway board is set to notify the SMVT Bengaluru-Mumbai CSMT Vande Bharat Sleeper soon. Sources state that the service will be flagged off later this month.The country's second Vande Bharat sleeper will significantly cut rail travel time between India's tech and financial capitals.According to the current plan, the flagship train will operate six days a week in both directions and will complete the journey in less than 16 hours. Currently, the Udyan Express, which is the only daily direct train between the cities, takes 24 hours on average.It could depart SMVT Bengaluru at 10 pm and reach CSMT Mumbai at 1:50 pm. In the return direction, the train could depart Mumbai at 10:30 pm and arrive in Bengaluru at 2:50 pm. Sources indicated that the timetable could change.While a flag-off date is yet to be announced, railway zones have been instructed to start it at an early, convenient date.The service will not pass through Hubballi; instead, it will have stoppages at Anantapur, Guntakal, Raichur, Kalaburagi, Solapur, and Kalyan.A superfast rail connectivity to Mumbai has been a demand that passengers have been raising for more than three decades. Despite promises, the travel between Mumbai and Bengaluru remains on the slower side. However, the announcement of the Vande Bharat Express is expected to ease and enhance the demand.
Article Summary: The country's second Vande Bharat sleeper will significantly cut rail travel time between India's tech and financial capitals. The flagship train will operate six days a week in both directions and will complete the journey in less than 16 hours. Currently, the Udyan Express, which is the only daily direct train between the cities, takes 24 hours on average.

Article Title: Adani Group plans Rs 6 lakh crore investment in Maharashtra; Rs 2.6 lakh crore projects underway
Article Text:
Pranav Adani said AEML provides electricity to over 3 million residential homes and establishments across Mumbai.

Adani Electricity

Aviation

Dharavi project

The Adani Group has completed or is currently executing projects worth at Rs 2.6 lakh crore in Maharashtra, Pranav Adani said on Thursday, during the launch of the state’s investment promotion agency, “Invest Maharashtra”.Speaking at the launch programme, Pranav Adani, who is Managing Director, Agro, Oil & Gas for Adani Group said the group’s planned investments in Maharashtra are worth more than Rs 6 lakh crore. The proposed projects cover a range of sectors, including energy, aviation and aero-districts, urban regeneration, data centres and coal gasification."At the World Economic Forum in Davos and through state partnerships, the Adani Group has committed to an investment blueprint exceeding 6 lakh crore rupees across critical and upcoming sectors like energy, aviation and aero-districts, urban regeneration, data centres and coal gasification. Projects worth 2.6 lakh crore rupees are already completed or under execution," he said according to an ET report.He noted that the Adani Group’s association with Maharashtra goes back several decades. However, its latest investment commitments mark a substantial expansion in the scale of its plans, as the state works towards its goal of becoming a one-trillion-dollar economy by 2030, with the Mumbai Metropolitan Region expected to be a key driver.Pranav Adani said Adani Electricity Mumbai Limited (AEML) provides electricity to over 3 million residential homes and establishments across Mumbai.He said renewable energy now accounts for over 60% of AEML’s electricity supply, and the company intends to raise this proportion to 70% or more.The Adani Group is also running a 1,000 MW High Voltage Direct Current (HVDC) transmission corridor to supply green electricity to Mumbai."And to insulate Mumbai’s financial core from outages, our 1,000 MW High Voltage Direct Current (HVDC) transmission link brings resilient, clean green power directly into the city," he said.Pranav Adani further said the group’s pumped-storage hydro projects in Maharashtra are designed to help ensure a continuous supply of green baseload power.Highlighting the group’s presence in Maharashtra’s aviation sector, Pranav Adani referred to the Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj International Airport (CSMIA), which it manages, as well as the greenfield Navi Mumbai International Airport."Alongside it, we are delivering the greenfield Navi Mumbai International Airport - a transformative infrastructure asset designed to anchor the Mumbai Metropolitan Region’s growth – and eventually handle over 90 million passengers annually," he said.The group is additionally building integrated airport-linked business and hospitality districts around both aviation hubs. Pranav Adani said these developments are intended to bring changes to urban mobility and commercial activity.Pranav Adani also spoke about the Dharavi Redevelopment Project, calling it a significant part of the group’s role in reshaping Mumbai’s urban landscape."Our approach is people-first: ensuring dignity, creating modern housing before relocation, formalising and safeguarding thousands of microenterprises - from leathercraft to pottery - and transforming Asia's largest informal settlement into a vibrant, integrated economic hub without displacing the community's soul," he said.He said the initiative is among the group’s contributions to “Mumbai 3.0”, envisaged as a metropolitan region that is better connected, more balanced and inclusive.According to Pranav Adani, the launch of Invest Maharashtra will create a platform to take investor interest beyond expressions of intent and translate it into projects on the ground."On behalf of the Adani Group, I reaffirm our unwavering commitment to stand shoulder-to-shoulder with the Government of Maharashtra and its hard-working people," he said.He said the group seeks to play a role in expanding Maharashtra’s industrial base while contributing to the state’s wider development goals. "Because when Maharashtra wins, India wins," he said.
Article Summary: The Adani Group has completed or is currently executing projects worth at Rs 2.6 lakh crore in Maharashtra. Pranav Adani said the group’s planned investments in Maharashtra are worth more than Rs 6 lakh crore. The proposed projects cover a range of sectors, including energy, aviation and aero-districts.

Article Title: Mumbai train alert: 75-day CSMT block from October 1; 8 long-distance trains short-terminated
Article Text:
Central Railway will implement a 75-day traffic and power block at Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus from October 1 (File photo)

Seven trains will be short-terminated at Dadar:

11002 Ballarshah-CSMT Nandigram Express

22120 Madgaon-CSMT Tejas Express

MUMBAI: Central Railway will impose another 75-day traffic and power block at Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus (CSMT) from October 1 to December 15 for the redevelopment of the heritage terminus, resulting in eight long-distance trains being short-terminated at Dadar and Thane.The block will cover platforms 14 and 15 and stabling line 15 and will be undertaken in connection with Phase-I of the CSMT redevelopment being executed by the Rail Land Development Authority (RLDA).Foundation work and other essential construction activities will be carried out during the block, with train operations from the two platforms suspended until the work is completed.The latest block comes after a prolonged closure of platforms 16 and 17 for the same redevelopment project.The earlier block began on February 1 and was initially scheduled for 85 days, till April 26. It was subsequently extended several times, with Central Railway saying the block continued until September 5.During this period, 10-14 long-distance trains were short-terminated at Dadar and Thane at different stages.The decision to take up work on platforms 14 and 15 had been a concern for Central Railway because these platforms handle another 16-18 long-distance services every day.CR had sought to have platforms 16 and 17 made fully operational before additional platforms were taken up for construction, citing the potential for further disruption to long-distance operations.The Rs 2,450-crore CSMT redevelopment project, approved by the Union cabinet in 2022, envisages transforming the terminus into an integrated transport hub while retaining the heritage character of its main Victorian Gothic building.The project includes new buildings, an elevated deck connecting platforms, improved passenger facilities and commercial spaces. The original completion deadline of March 2026 has been extended to October 2028.On completion of the current block, RLDA will hand over platforms 14 and 15 for train operations, Central Railway said.Passengers travelling on the affected trains have been advised to plan their journeys accordingly.
Article Summary: Central Railway will impose another 75-day traffic and power block at Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus (CSMT) from October 1 to December 15. Eight long-distance trains will be short-terminated at Dadar and Thane. The block will cover platforms 14 and 15 and stabling line 15.
